description:
I'm a Mathematics and Data Science student interested in AI/ML, Physics, Robotics, and Space Exploration. I have experience with Python, NumPy, Pandas, data analysis, and visualization. I'm excited to develop an interactive space survival game that combines technology, science, and creativity.

I'm looking for teammates skilled in Game Development, Web Development, AI/ML, UI/UX Design, and Physics. I'm eager to collaborate, learn, share ideas, and build something innovative together!
summary:
Project NEXOVOID is “Moon Base Commander,” an interactive 2D game built in the Godot Engine as our response to the “Build a Junior Astronaut Mission Trainer” challenge. The game is designed for children aged 7 to 12 and lets them step into the role of a junior astronaut exploring a lunar base. Players control an astronaut on the Moon’s surface using simple keyboard controls, making the experience easy to learn for young users.

Our goal is to make space exploration feel exciting and approachable. Instead of reading about missions in a textbook, children learn by playing, which builds curiosity about space, science, and teamwork. The game uses real lunar imagery to give players a sense of what the Moon looks like.

This matters because early interest in STEM often begins with play. By turning mission training into a fun, hands-on experience, NEXOVOID inspires the next generation of astronauts, engineers, and scientists. The project is built to be expanded with more missions, challenges, and learning activities.
details:
What it does: Moon Base Commander is a 2D game for children aged 7 to 12 where players take the role of a junior astronaut on the Moon. The player controls an astronaut on a lunar surface using the keyboard, which keeps the experience simple and easy to learn.

Benefits and impact: The game makes space exploration fun and approachable. By learning through play, children build curiosity about space, science, and teamwork, which can inspire interest in STEM.

Tools used: The game was built in the Godot Engine (version 4.7.2) using GDScript, with lunar imagery for the background and an astronaut character.

Creativity: Instead of a textbook approach, we turned astronaut training into an interactive game that kids can play directly.

Factors we considered: Simple controls, kid-friendly visuals, and a design that can be expanded with more missions and challenges.
